analysis.investment_thesis: Anlon fits the SMILE shell — 616 Cr micro-cap API maker with 52.7% promoter holding, ROCE of 38%, and EBITDA growing at 77% CAGR. But four straight years of negative operating cash flow (-23 Cr in FY25 vs 21 Cr PAT) and lumpy revenue (57→113→67→120) mean I want to see cash conversion before committing real capital.
key_strengths: Sweet-spot size: 616 Cr micro-cap in a multi-thousand-crore global API TAM
Stellar unit economics: 33.7% OPM, 25.5% ROE, 38.1% ROCE with D/E just 0.27
EBITDA CAGR 77%, Revenue CAGR 28%, promoter holding 52.68% — aspiration + skin in game
key_risks: OCF negative 4/4 years; FY25 OCF -23 Cr vs PAT +21 Cr — working capital black hole
Revenue is erratic (dropped 113→67 in FY24) suggesting customer/order concentration
Cash only 1 Cr vs debt 67 Cr; growth is being funded by IPO equity (21→80 Cr jump)
red_flags: Profits on paper but zero cash generation — receivables/inventory bloat needs explanation
FII at 0.32% and thin float post-IPO — price discovery still immature
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the surface this is a textbook Kedia candidate: small Rajkot-based API/nutraceutical/veterinary intermediate maker, 12 years old (medium experience), promoter at 52.7%, operating in a secular India-pharma-export theme. Margins are extraordinary for a company this size (33.7% OPM, 38% ROCE), growth is accelerating (EBITDA 6→13→16→32 Cr), and P/E of 17.75 on a still-scaling base isn't demanding if FY26 doubles again. The transformation catalyst — recent IPO capital (equity jumped 21→80 Cr), debt deleveraging in FY25, and global regulatory filings — is visible.

What stops me short is the cash flow statement. Zero positive OCF years in the last four, and FY25 actually worsened to -23 Cr despite record PAT — classic sign of receivables/inventory being inflated to book revenue. For a small API player this could simply be export credit cycles, but it could also be aggressive revenue recognition. I'd hold off until I see one clean year of OCF ≥ PAT, evidence that top-5 customer concentration is below 40%, and clarity on whether the FY23→FY24 revenue drop was a one-off. At 115 with P/E 17.75, I'm not getting a margin of safety for those unknowns.
